scope: Selected excerpts from SQLite's public-domain documentation, read through Sibyl. These are not complete pages or independent publishers. Replay timestamps describe replay, not a fresh fetch.

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.section: 1. Overview; 9. Sometimes Queries Return SQLITE_BUSY In WAL Mode
sources.text:
WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed concurrently.

All processes using a database must be on the same host computer; WAL does not work over a network filesystem.

But there are some obscure cases where a query against a WAL-mode database can return SQLITE_BUSY, so applications should be prepared for that happenstance.

sources.title: Isolation In SQLite
sources.section: Isolation Between Database Connections; Isolation And Concurrency
sources.text:
SQLite implements serializable transactions by actually serializing the writes. There can only be a single writer at a time to an SQLite database. There can be multiple database connections open at the same time, and all of those database connections can write to the database file, but they have to take turns.

WAL mode permits simultaneous readers and writers.

In WAL mode, SQLite exhibits snapshot isolation. When a read transaction starts, that reader continues to see an unchanging snapshot of the database file as it existed at the moment in time when the read transaction started.
